findings.description: The bucket defines no server_side_encryption_configuration, so objects (including the seeded vendor roster) are stored without enforced SSE-KMS encryption.
No ACL is set and no aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is attached, so the bucket can be made public through ACLs or bucket policies without guardrails.
The bucket has no logging block, so object-level access to archived reports is not recorded for audit or forensic purposes.
Versioning is not enabled and force_destroy is true, so objects can be overwritten or destroyed without any recoverable prior version, aiding tampering or ransomware-style deletion.
The ledger export bucket has no server_side_encryption_configuration, leaving financial export data unencrypted at rest by default.
No logging block is configured for the ledger bucket, so reads and writes of sensitive ledger data leave no audit trail.
Versioning is disabled while force_destroy is true, so ledger export objects can be silently overwritten or deleted with no recovery path.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block is associated with this bucket, so a later ACL or policy change could expose ledger data publicly without any account-level guardrail.
Model artifact bucket lacks server_side_encryption_configuration; artifacts are stored without enforced encryption, and unsigned/unencrypted artifacts are a supply-chain tampering risk.
No public access block is attached, leaving the bucket's exposure dependent on ACL/policy configuration that can drift.
Runbooks frequently contain operational details, endpoints, and occasionally credentials; this bucket has no server-side encryption configuration.
No logging block is defined, so access to operational runbooks is not audited.
No aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block guards this bucket against accidental public ACLs or policies.
The audit/log-delivery bucket sets force_destroy = true and has no public access block or MFA-delete/object-lock protection, allowing the audit trail to be destroyed and undermining log integrity.

findings.issue_category: missing access logging on log bucket
findings.description: The audit bucket does not log access to itself, so tampering with or exfiltration of collected logs is not recorded.

A vendor roster spreadsheet is uploaded from the repository into a bucket that has no default encryption, and the object itself specifies no kms_key_id or server_side_encryption, so potentially sensitive third-party data is stored in plaintext and committed to version control.
